title: Vowel-shifted heading over a Latin poem, Ambrosiana A 118 inf. f. 154r (catalogue #1347)

steps.what: Fetched f. 154r from the Ambrosiana IIIF manifest (canvas 319).
Read the heading and transcribed the 16-line poem; the body is plain Latin, only the heading word is enciphered.
Vowel shift to the next letter (a>b, e>f, i>l, o>p, u>x) from the absence of a, i, u and the repeated f, p, l.
Undid the shift: ?-e-n-o-e-i-?-e-o with r or x in seventh place; also full Caesar +1 (no word).
Web searches on the incipit and lines of the poem; OPAC record read for an attribution.
Google Books snippet search found a 1989 Macerata Annali article (p. 872) that transcribes the heading and a second cipher group and calls both undeciphered.

outcome.method_basis: The vowel-shift mechanism fits the nine-letter heading word, but undoing it gives no Latin or Italian name, and the glyphs are ambiguous at the available image size.
outcome.notes: Needs the poem's attribution from other manuscripts or a better image of the heading.

prior.where: Annali della Facolta di Lettere e Filosofia (Macerata) vols 22-23, 1989, p. 872: the cipher groups were transcribed and left 'non decifrate' (Google Books snippet; article not seen)

human: Gave the catalogue number and asked for it to be solved and written up; no target-specific intervention.
